curation_order: Download repository bytes into memory only; verify publisher checksum and size before parsing.
Read URL and ClassLabel only; quarantine missing-label rows, reject nonmissing unknown labels, invert documented numeric 0/1 to project schema.

Use frozen v6 prepare_url in memory. Reject unsupported input and additional sensitive path assignments if experimental privacy guard would change the frozen core. Do not persist raw URLs or silently change representation.
Quarantine all scheme-free representations with conflicting publisher labels, then retain lowest original row number per consistent representation.

Exclude previously exposed canonical URL hashes, scheme-free representation hashes and domain/private-tenant hashes against the historical registry plus current v6 caches. Audit exclusion counts and class support.
Cap each remaining registered domain/private tenant at five rows, ordered by canonical digest without model scores or labels.

Freeze sanitized cache, counts, source/code/protocol and exposure hashes before any predictions. Keep all supported intake hashes in a separate local append-only exposure sidecar; never overwrite the historical registry.
scoring: Original frozen v6 and both original thresholds only. No fitting, tuning, calibration fitting, threshold selection or candidate comparison.
limitations: Publisher methods mix manual review and threat-feed matching; no claim that all rows had two independent human reviews.
The dataset includes URLhaus provenance; phishing-vs-malware scope and per-case labels remain unverified.
Shared upstream sources may cause overlap even though this release has not been evaluated by this run.
Domain-disjoint and hash-disjoint filtering does not establish campaign independence or correct labels.
Unknown collection timestamps and absence of verified Indonesia relevance prevent temporal/Indonesia claims.
Privacy heuristics are not proof of full anonymization; no raw targets are persisted or visited.
